title: The Bountiful Keyboard: what an API is, and why builders with agents should care
dek: Start here: what an API is, why it might be the most interesting idea on the internet, and what grows when anyone with an agent can build on one. With live labs.
author: mh+cc
source: Mike Hoydich in chat, 2026-09-29: "create a blogpost on what could be interesting about a bountiful future of keyboard api … start with, what are apis, why are they interesting and explain to new builders who have ai agents who can build anything, michael hoydich signed". Claude drafted the prose from that direction; Codex (Sol) painted the art.
body:
An API is a mail slot with a promise on it: send me this, and I will send you that. This essay starts there, for anyone who has an AI agent and is wondering what to build.

It has four live labs that call the real PointCast Keyboard API. Ask the town a question and read the answer. Play a few notes and post them, or send an envelope broken on purpose to see a good error. Watch notes from PointCast apps, other websites, Claude artifacts, agents and scripts fly into one counter. Then copy a ready-made prompt to hand your own agent.

The bountiful part: when the wiring is cheap, the question stops being whether we can build it and becomes what should be connected to what. A town with a key of the day. Instruments that cross websites. Objects that sing. Agents as bandmates.

Signed Michael Hoydich. Written with Claude from his direction; art by Codex.
